# sideby

> Run every AI coding account side by side. sideby is a Node CLI (npm package `sideby`, Node 22.18+) that starts Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build and pi with one isolated config directory per account, keeps skills, hooks and rules shared with the Main Account, repairs drift with `doctor`, and shows each account's quota from local records or the official Host CLI, and 7-day token usage from local records (built in; no ccusage).

Key facts:

- One account = one directory. claude: `~/.claude` (main), `~/.claude-<name>`, selected by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. codex: `~/.codex`, `~/.codex-<name>`, `CODEX_HOME`. grok: `~/.grok`, `~/.grok-<name>`, `GROK_HOME`. pi: `~/.pi/agent`, `~/.pi-<name>/agent`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. agy (Antigravity CLI): `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` only, a Main-only Family (`mainOnly: true` in `sideby families --json`, ADR-0047): agy has no variable that moves its config or sign-in, so `sideby new agy …` is refused (`code: family-main-only`) and nothing is written. The Main Account is named `main` and runs without the variable.
- Account ref: `<family>:<name>`; a bare `<name>` works when unique. Names match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`.
- Discovery: a directory matching the pattern is an account only if it holds `proxy.env` or at least one of the family's Shared Items (so `~/.claude-code-router` is not an account). Config `ignore` skips refs.
- API account: an account directory containing `proxy.env` (dotenv subset, mode exactly 600). Its variables reach only the launched Host. Login state is `not-needed` (`key` in `sideby list`). Exception: pi loads `proxy.env` for provider keys, but a pi account stays a subscription account and signs in with `/login`.
- sideby never switches a global active account, never reads credentials to call a model, never proxies or pools logins, and never calls private quota endpoints. `sideby next` only recommends the next account from local quota data; a person starts it. Only Auto Handoff (config `handoff.auto`, off by default; ADR-0010) moves a running task to another account by itself.
- Agents must not read `proxy.env`, `auth.json` or `.claude.json`, and must let the user run `sideby login <ref>` themselves. sideby itself reads only identity fields there (email, Claude organization; the `email` claim of Codex's `id_token`), never a token value (ADR-0003); `sideby list` shows them.
- What a new account shares (`sideby families <family> --json` gives the same for the user's machine, plugin families and config `extraSharedItems` included). claude: links `settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, `skills`, `commands`, `plugins`, `hooks`, `themes`, `CLAUDE.md`; keeps only the `mcpServers` entry of its own `.claude.json` equal to `~/.claude.json`. codex: links `AGENTS.md`, `hooks.json`, `plugins`, `rules`, `skills`; `config.toml` linked (or a synced copy) for subscription accounts, the account's own for API accounts. grok: links `skills`, `installed-plugins`; copies `hooks`, `hooks-paths` and a subscription account's `config.toml` (Grok refuses links there); `trusted_folders.toml` is copied once, then the account's own. pi: links `AGENTS.md`. agy: nothing (main account only). Never shared: sign-in (`auth.json`, Keychain, the rest of `.claude.json`), sessions and history. Items the Main Account lacks are skipped.

## Set up sideby for a user

Users ask "install sideby", "set up another Claude account, cc008". Do every step yourself except those marked **user**; for those, give the user exactly one line to run (in Claude Code they can type `! <command>`).

1. `node --version` must be 22.18 or newer; otherwise tell the user to upgrade Node and stop. npm's `engines` warning (`EBADENGINE`) does not stop the program. sideby exits 1 itself below 22.18, including `--help` and `--version`; `statusline-tap` still runs the original status-line command. `sideby --version`; if it is missing, `npm i -g sideby` (a global install is needed for Claude quota and shell functions).
2. `npx skills add Adonis0123/sideby -g` installs the sideby skill so later requests go through it.
3. `sideby list --json`: `families[].installed` says which Host CLIs are on PATH. For a Host that is not installed, give the user its `installCommand` (an official one-line installer, when the Family has one) or its `installUrl`, and stop; never install a Host unasked. `brokenBin` means the Host is on PATH but cannot run (often a link left by an interrupted upgrade): reinstalling fixes it. If the Host has no Main Account yet, ask the user to start it once (for example `claude`); `new` needs the Main Account.
4. `sideby families <family> --json`: tell the user in a sentence or two what the new account will share and that its sign-in, sessions and history stay its own.
5. Create it. With a name from the user: `sideby new <family> <name> --json`. Without one: `sideby new <family> --next --json`, which picks the next number (`008` after `001`…`007`) and a short command following the existing ones (`cc008`; see `suggestion`). Add `--alias <short>` when the user named a short command, and `--api` for an API account.
6. **user**: subscription account: `sideby login <ref>` (browser sign-in; for pi it starts pi, then they type `/login`). API account: the user fills in the `proxy.env` path that `new` printed; never read or write it yourself.
7. Make short commands work in new terminals: when the config has no `shellInitFile` and the user's `~/.zshrc` (bash: `~/.bashrc`) has no `sideby shell-init` line, say so and append `eval "$(sideby shell-init zsh)"` (or `bash`) to it.
8. Verify: `sideby doctor <ref> --json` (`status: "ok"`), and after the user signed in, `sideby list --json` shows `login: "logged-in"` for the account.
9. Optional, Claude only, when the user wants quota: `sideby quota setup claude` exits 10 with a diff; show it, and only after a yes run it again with `--yes`.

Finish by telling the user how to start it: the short command in a new terminal, or `sideby run <ref>`.

## Commands

- `sideby` / `sideby list [--json]`: list accounts (TYPE `main`|`sub`|`api`, LOGIN `✓`|`login needed`|`key`|`?`, EMAIL, MODEL, DIR, and on macOS DESKTOP `open` when that account's desktop app window runs). `--json` accounts carry optional `identity: { email?, org? }` and `sameLogin: [ref]`: the other accounts signed in as the same login (same email and organization; Codex also the same ChatGPT workspace, Grok the same x.ai user and team), which share one quota (spec §3.21); the table marks them as `claude:001 = main`. Problems plugins hit while reading an account go to stderr. Exit 0.
- `sideby run <acct> [-- args]`: start the Host for one account. Exit: Host's code; 128+n if killed by signal n; 1 on sideby error. Argument order: family defaults, the family's `keepTitle` args (only with config `accountTitle`), `accounts.<ref>.args` from config, the alias's `args` when `<acct>` is an alias, then user args. The Host gets `SIDEBY_ACCOUNT=<ref>` and `SIDEBY_LABEL` (the alias it was started through; else the account's alias, those without args first; else the ref) for a status line or prompt; both are set on every launch (`run`, `next`, `login`, a routed `resume`). With config `accountTitle: true` the terminal title becomes `[<SIDEBY_LABEL>]` and Codex gets `-c tui.terminal_title=[]` so it keeps it. Claude Code 2.1.287+ (version from `claude --version`, cached per binary in `<state>/cache/claude-version.json`) also gets `--plugin-dir <package>/mods/claude` before the first `--`, after every `launch.before` hook, unless `-p`/`--print` or config `claudeMod: false`: sideby's mod shows the Session Label above the prompt, a toast for an arriving sideby Message, and `/sessions` (a pane from `sideby sessions --json` with copy buttons); it writes nothing.
- `sideby new <family> <name>|--next [--api] [--alias <short>] [--json]`: create an account. `--next` picks the name instead: the next number after the highest numbered account with the same width (`001`…`007` → `008`), else `work`, `work2`, …; without `--alias` it also adds a short command when the family's existing aliases show a prefix-plus-name pattern (`cc007` for `claude:007` → `cc008`), and leaves it out, with the reason in `suggestion.aliasProblem`, when that name is taken or reserved. A name together with `--next` exits 2. `--alias` also adds `<short> → <family>:<name>` to config `aliases` (sideby writes only `aliases` and `handoff` in the config: `aliases` here and in `sideby alias`, `handoff` in `sideby handoff enable|disable`; keys and order kept, refused when the config is not valid JSON); an invalid, reserved or taken alias is refused before anything is created. After creating, every configured `shellInitFile` is rewritten. Exit 0; 1 partly failed, invalid name, or the alias was not added (the account still exists).
- `sideby alias add <short> <acct> [-- host args] [--json]`: add a short command for an existing account. `<acct>` may be a ref, a unique name or an alias; the config stores the ref, as a string, or as `{ account, args }` when host args follow `--`. Only `sideby run <short>` adds those args; other commands just resolve the account. Rewrites every `shellInitFile`. Exit 0 (`status` `added`, or `exists` when identical); 1 when the name is invalid or reserved, the account does not exist, or the name already starts something else (remove it first). `sideby alias rm <short> [--json]`: exit 0 (`removed` or `absent`); it removes a pick command too. Aliases never carry environment variables.
- `sideby alias add <short> --pick <family> [--yes] [--json]`: a Pick Command (config `pickCommands`, ADR-0035), one namespace with `aliases`. `sideby run <short>` (and the shell function) starts the account `sideby next <family>` would pick and prints `<short> → <ref> (…)` to stderr; with no quota data in the family it starts the main account; with data but nothing usable it starts nothing (exit 1). Never the Host's own name. Without `--yes` it returns `status: "confirm"` (with `shadows` when the name is a command on PATH) and exit 10. Without a signed-in subscription main it falls back to the pick, never to an API account. `sideby alias list [--json]`: `{ shortCommands: [{ name, kind: "account"|"pick", account?, args?, family? }] }`. `sideby new` returns `pickCommandOffer` once, when a family gets its second subscription account.
- `sideby shell-init setup [zsh|bash] [--yes|--undo] [--json]` (ADR-0036): `{ shell, rc, status: "loaded"|"confirm"|"added"|"removed"|"not-added", block? }`. Appends a marked `eval "$(sideby shell-init <shell>)"` block to `$ZDOTDIR/.zshrc` / `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc` (exit 10 until `--yes`), only when nothing there loads sideby and no `shellInitFile` is set; `--undo` removes only that block.
- `sideby login <acct>`: run the family's sign-in command with the account selected; for pi, start pi and print "type /login". Before it, stderr says who the account is signed in as (and its same login); after it, whether the account now has a login of its own or is still the same login (the browser reused its login: sign out there or use a private window, then run it again). Also the way to switch an account to another login; nothing is signed out first. Exit: Host's code.
- `sideby next <family> [--dry-run] [--include-api] [--json] [-- host args]`: Handoff. Rank the family's accounts by Quota Pressure (used percent of the fullest window not reset yet) and start the lowest, as `sideby run` would. States: `ready` (subscription, under 85%), `unknown` (no quota data; ranked after ready), `api` (only with `--include-api`), `full` (a live window at 85%+), `logged-out`. `--dry-run` and `--json` only recommend. When no account has quota data (`hasQuota: false`) nothing starts and the exit code is 1. Claude and Codex; families without a quota source fail with code `no-quota-source` and list their accounts. Exit: Host's code when started; 0 for `--dry-run`/`--json` with a pick; 1 when nothing can be picked, no account has quota data, no quota source or no accounts. The new account starts a new session; sessions are not copied. Accounts of the same login share one quota; run inside a session sideby started (`SIDEBY_ACCOUNT`), `next` never picks an account of that session's same login.
- `sideby doctor [acct|family] [--fix] [--force] [--json]`: check Shared Items, credential modes, leftovers, and whether the sideby skill each checked family's Host reads (`<main>/skills/sideby`, plus `~/.agents/skills/sideby` for Codex) matches this version (`skill.outdated`, general warn on that family's main account). Exit 0 when no `fail` Finding (warnings allowed); 1 otherwise.
- `sideby quota [acct|family] [--refresh] [--json]`: quota windows and 7-day usage, in the Display Order. Grok quota (spec §3.26, ADR-0025) is asked from the `grok` CLI of each signed-in subscription account (`grok agent --no-leader stdio`, method `_x.ai/billing`; the Host sends the request with its own login, sideby reads no credential), at most every 15 minutes per account and kept in `<state>/quota/<family>/<name>.fetched.json`; the newer of that and the Grok log's billing line is shown; `--refresh` asks again now; off with config `quota.check.<family>: false` or in CI (`reason: not-enabled`). A failed ask is `reason: fetch-failed` with `detail`, or `fetchError` on the last good reading (`fetched: true`). A window may carry `name` (models it covers, such as a plugin's "Other models"); named windows do not count toward Quota Pressure. Accounts of the same login show the freshest reading of the login, with `from: <ref>` when it was read from another account; usage stays per account. Exit 0.
- `sideby quota setup claude [--yes] [--json]`: without `--yes`, print the diff and change nothing; with `--yes`, wrap `statusLine.command` in `~/.claude/settings.json` as `sideby statusline-tap --orig-b64 <base64>` (or `sideby statusline-tap` when there was none). Refused (exit 1) if `sideby` is not on PATH or comes from the npx cache: needs `npm i -g sideby`. Exit 10 when it only showed the change (rerun with `--yes` after the user agrees); 0 applied or already enabled; 1 blocked or failed.
- `sideby tune [acct|family] [--json]`: estimate the cheapest auto-compact threshold per model from the last 7 days of local session records. Claude gets a suggested `autoCompactWindow`; Codex only observations; Grok and pi no source. An estimate; nothing changes until `sideby tune apply <acct> [tokens] [--yes] [--json]` (without `--yes` it prints the file, the change and which accounts share the file, and exits 10; show it to the user and only then rerun with `--yes`; writes one key, `autoCompactWindow`, of the account's `settings.json`) and `sideby tune undo <acct> [--yes]`. Exit 0; 1 unknown account or family, blocked, nothing to undo; 2 extra arguments.
- `sideby model <acct> [<model>|default] [--effort <level>|default] [--yes] [--json]` (spec §3.19): the model and effort the account runs with, each `{ value, from }` with `from`, first match wins, `sideby` (the account's arguments in the config), `last` (the newest session) or `host` (Claude `settings.json` `model` / `modelSettings.<model>.effortLevel` / `effortLevel`; Codex `config.toml` `model` / `model_reasoning_effort`); a change edits only the model and effort arguments in config `accounts.<ref>.args` (exit 10 without `--yes`); never writes a Host file; not for API accounts.
- `sideby remote-control [on|off|undo] [--yes] [--json]` (spec §3.22, ADR-0017): each Claude settings file (accounts linking to one file share it) with `state` on (`remoteControlAtStartup` true: sessions connect to claude.ai/code and the Claude app by themselves), default (not set), off, missing (no settings.json: run `sideby doctor --fix`), blocked. `off` writes `remoteControlAtStartup: false` into every on or default file, one key only; `on` writes `true` into every off or default file (only when the user asks: every device signed in to the account can then read new sessions); `undo` restores the old value while the key still holds what sideby wrote. Without `--yes` each prints the change and exits 10; show it to the user first. `/remote-control` in a session still works; running sessions stay connected until restarted. Exit 0 done; 1 nothing to change (`ok` false, message says it is already on or off), blocked, failed or nothing to undo; 2 bad arguments.
- `sideby quota teardown claude [--json]`: restore the original bytes, only if the file is unchanged since setup; otherwise refuse with a diff. Exit 0; 1 refused or failed.
- `sideby ui [--port n] [--no-open]`: local panel on `127.0.0.1:17420`; reuses a running sideby panel, shifts past busy ports.
- `sideby ui --background [--port n] [--no-open]`: start the panel detached from the terminal (pid and log in the state directory; Hosts found through the login shell's PATH), or reuse a running one (replaced when it runs another build, so an upgrade takes effect), then open it. An open panel page reloads itself when the server runs another build (`build` in `/api/state`). `sideby ui --stop`: stop it, only after checking the pid is a sideby panel. Exit 0; 1 if it could not start or stop.
- `sideby desktop <acct> [--json]` (spec §3.20, macOS only): open the Family's Desktop App as that account: Claude Desktop (bundle id `com.anthropic.claudefordesktop`) for claude, the Codex app (`ChatGPT.app`, `com.openai.codex`) for codex. The Main Account opens with `open -n -a <app>` (the default data folder); any other subscription account with `open -n`, its select variable (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME`, plus `CODEX_ELECTRON_USER_DATA_PATH`) and `--user-data-dir` at `~/Library/Application Support/sideby/<family>/<name>/` (mode 700). An account whose window already runs is brought to the front (`action: "focused"`, or `already-running`), never started twice; sideby never ends a process, never modifies the app bundle, writes nothing into Host account dirs. A new Claude app data folder gets `claude_desktop_config.json` linked to the Main Account's default one (Doctor checks it as `app-data/claude_desktop_config.json` under `link` rules, except that a real file there, which the app writes itself, is checked only for its `mcpServers` key under `json-key` rules, as `app-data/claude_desktop_config.json#mcpServers`). Agent-session variables (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, `CODEX_COMPANION_*`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX*`) are cleared before `open`. A new account's sign-in screen may suggest the main account ("Welcome back" in the Codex app); tell the user to choose another account. Output `{ ref, family, app, appPath, action, appData?, createdAppData, linked[], command?, notices[] }`; relay `notices` (first sign-in: close other Claude Desktop windows). Exit 0; 1 with code `not-macos`, `no-desktop-app`, `api-account`, `app-not-installed`, `open-failed`; 2 missing argument.
- `sideby desktop grok-bot[:<name>] [--remove [--yes]] [--json]` (spec §3.20 "Grok Bot 窗口", ADR-0019, macOS only): Grok Bot (`Grok Bot.app`, `com.anysphere.sand`) signs in with a Cursor account, apart from every Account (not Grok Build), so its windows are App Profiles, not Accounts. `grok-bot:<name>` opens that window, creating `~/Library/Application Support/sideby/grok-bot/<name>/` (mode 700) first when the name is new; `grok-bot` / `grok-bot:main` is the app's default data. Opens with `open -n -a <app> --args --user-data-dir=<folder>`, `SAND_DATA_ROOT` / `SAND_USER_DATA_DIR` cleared; a running window is brought to the front. Same output as `desktop` (`family: "grok-bot"`); bad name `code: invalid-name`. `--remove` without `--yes` exits 10 with `{ ref, app, appData, removed: false }`, with `--yes` deletes the folder (`removed: true`); refuses `main-profile`, `app-running` (also when `ps` fails), `no-profile`, `app-data-invalid` (a link or file; never followed). `sideby list --json` has top-level `appProfiles: [{ ref, app, name, isMain, appData?, installed, running, signedIn? }]`; `signedIn` is the app's own `desktop-status.json` flag (last known), the signed-in email is never read. `sideby desktop grok:<acct>` is `no-desktop-app` and points at `grok-bot:<name>`.
- `sideby sessions [<acct>|<family>] [--json]` (spec §3.32, ADR-0039): Live Sessions of every account, read-only from the Hosts' own non-credential files and the running processes (`ps`; `lsof` for Codex): Claude `<dir>/sessions/<pid>.json` (skipped when the pid is gone or its `procStart` differs; never deleted), Grok `<dir>/active_sessions.json` (pid and `pid_start`), Codex the `rollout-*.jsonl` a `codex` process with that `CODEX_HOME` holds open, pi the newest session file of an account with a running `pi`; where sideby cannot tie a process to a session (Codex, pi) it takes the newest one with `guessed: true`. Output `{ sessions: [{ account, accountLabel, family, sessionId, title, label, status: needs-you|busy|idle|unknown, cwd?, pid?, startedAt?, updatedAt?, guessed, transcript?, reference, resumeCommand }], problems[] }`, `needs-you` first, then by most recent activity. `label` is the Session Label `<accountLabel> · <the Host's own title, else the cwd name> · <first 8 of id>`; `reference` the Session Reference in English. `run?` `{ title, laneTitle?, role?, board, url, others? }` (ADR-0041): the Run a local orchestrator ties the session to, from its optional Session Index (`$AGENT_DISPATCH_STATE_DIR/session-index.json`, else `$XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-dispatch/session-index.json`, else `~/.local/state/agent-dispatch/session-index.json`; `schemaVersion` 1, at most 256 KB, not a link; `sessions.<id>.entries[]` of `{ run, runTitle, board, lane, laneTitle, role, url }`). An entry counts only when `board` is a regular `.html` file of the user, not a link, right inside `<state>/boards/`, and `url` is exactly `file://<board>` with an optional `#lane-<id>`. With several, the first by role (coordinator, write, review, research, other) is `run` and the rest `others` (each with `board`); opening checks the board and its folder once more (not links, owner, device and inode unchanged) right before the program starts. No network request. The table adds a `RUN` column and a `Run: <title>  <board path>` line per checked board, each once; the Panel's chip opens the board with the default program (read-only Panel: hidden). Exit 0; 1 unknown account or family.
- `sideby sessions open-run <acct|session-id> [--json]` (ADR-0041): open the Run Board of the session's `run` with the default program, through the same checks and opener as the Panel's `/api/sessions/run` (board found again from the Session Index, checked once more right before the program starts, never a path from the caller). The session is picked as `sessions copy` picks it. Output `{ opened: true, board, sessionId, label }` (`board` with `~`). Exit 0; 1 with code `no-session`, `several-sessions`, `no-run` (not in a Run, or its board is gone), `board-changed` or `open-failed`.
- `sideby sessions copy <acct|session-id> [--as reference|id|resume] [--lang en|zh] [--json]`: put one session's Session Reference (default; one sentence with the account, Label, cwd and the path of its record, never the conversation), its id, or `resumeCommand` on the clipboard (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, `xclip`; none: the text is printed, `copied: false`). `--lang` defaults to the locale. Output `{ copied, as, text, sessionId, label }`. Exit 0; 1 with code `no-session`, or `several-sessions` when the account runs several (the message lists `sideby sessions copy <id>` for each). With config `accountTitle`, the tab title of a Host sideby started grows from `[cc002]` to `[<Session Label>]` once its session shows up, checked every 10 s.
- `sideby history [<words>...] [--project <path|name>] [--family <id>] [--account <acct>] [--since today|7d|30d|all] [--category <name>] [--group project|category|account|family|day|none] [--scripts] [--tools] [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>] [--json]` (spec §3.33, ADR-0042, ADR-0044): Session History, every past session of every account, read-only from the Hosts' own records (Claude `projects/*/<id>.jsonl` and `<id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, Codex `sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and `session_index.jsonl`, Grok `sessions/<cwd>/<id>/summary.json` and `chat_history.jsonl`, pi `sessions/*/*.jsonl`), never a credential file. Project: the git root above the session's `cwd` (a worktree's `.git` file folds into its main repository; a gone folder keeps Grok's `git_root_dir`, else itself). Session Title: the user's name, else the Host's title, else the first prompt. Every word must match; a quoted `"two words"` is one phrase (title, project, branch, account, typed prompts, replies; FTS5 trigram for 3+ characters, LIKE for 1–2); best match first (relevance times a recency boost halving every 7 days), else newest first. Script Sessions (Claude `entrypoint` `sdk*` and subagents, Codex non-`cli`/`vscode` `source`, Grok non-empty `session_kind`) only with `--scripts`; subagents count for their parent. `--tools` also scans the record files in scope for the words, tool output included, keeping nothing; those sessions come after the indexed ones, on the last page, with `foundIn: "tools"`, and `toolOutputMore: true` when a full page held them back. `--project` takes a name or a folder (`.`, `..`, `~`, absolute), resolved to its git root. `--limit` 1–500 (default 30), `--offset` pages on. Output `{ sessions: [{ account, accountLabel, family, sessionId, title, titleFrom: user|host|prompt|none, project, projectName, cwd, cwdGone?, branch?, model?, startedAt, updatedAt, messages, script, parent?, children, snippet?, live, transcript, resumeCommand, continueCommand, reference }], total, index: { state: building|ready|off|unavailable, progress: { done, total } }, sources: [{ account, accountLabel, family, sessions, files, failed, note? }], problems[] }`; `continueCommand` is `cd <cwd> && <resumeCommand>` (only `resumeCommand` when the folder is gone). `history show <id> [--account <acct>] [--before <n>] [--limit <n>]` (id or 8+ leading characters; `--account` picks one when two accounts share the id): `{ session, messages: [{ n, role: user|assistant|tool, text, at?, tool? }], before? }`, the newest 200 by default, tool calls as their name only. `--group` (not with `--tools`) adds `groups: [{ key, label, sessions, updatedAt, collapsed? }]` (best group first, the one without a key last; days in time order) and `group` on each session. A plugin may sort projects into categories (`PluginApi.projectCategories`, first plugin only, answers kept 1 minute, 3 s timeout): then `categories: { label, from }` and `--category <name>` filters; without one `--category` exits 1. A plugin Family gives its own reader as `FamilyDef.history` (`list`, `parse`, `messages`, `toolText?`, `titles?`, `resumeArgs`); without it its accounts' `sources` say `reason: unsupported`. `history projects`: `{ projects: [{ project, name, sessions, updatedAt, gone?, category? }], categories? }`. `history index [--clear]`: `{ enabled, path, state, progress, files, sessions, bytes, sources, cleared? }`. The History Index is `<state>/history/index.sqlite` (`node:sqlite`, folder 700, file 600): per record file its size, mtime and inode, per session the fields above and the text of typed prompts and replies, never tool calls or output, injected context, reasoning or Codex `session_meta` account ids and instructions. Config `history.index` (default true): false stops and deletes it, and only titles and folders are searched. If the index file cannot be opened an in-memory index is used and `problems` says why; without `node:sqlite` the result says to upgrade Node. Exit 0; 1 unknown session, project, category or account, or an id several sessions match; 2 malformed flags.
- `sideby send <acct|session> "<text>" [--image <path>]... [--lang en|zh] [--json]` (spec §3.32 step 2, ADR-0040): send a Message to one Live Session (an account with exactly one running session, a session id, or its first 8 characters; several: exit 1 with code `several-sessions` listing `sideby send <id> "<text>"`). The Message is first kept as `<state>/messages/<session id>/<time>-<id>.md` (mode 600, folders 700; a small header with From, To, Sent, then the text) with each screenshot copied next to it (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP by their first bytes, at most 20 MB; anything else: exit 1, code `bad-image`, nothing written) and a `.json` receipt. A Claude Code session then gets it through Claude Code's own cross-session channel: one line `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":…}}` written to the socket its `sessions/<pid>.json` names (`messagingSocketPath`), only when that socket is in `cc-socks` (or this user's `cc-socks-<uid>`) right inside `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or a system temp folder, owned by the user and not a link, the folder not open to others, and the process still runs that session; no token is sent and the `<pid>.<hash>.key` files are never opened; it reads the record and processes again right before connecting, and after connecting checks that the socket and its folder are the same files (device, inode, owner) before writing; 3 s timeout; the connection is closed once the line is flushed. Message folders are checked one at a time (real folders of the user, not links, not writable by others; never `.` or `..`); screenshots are copied from the file that was checked, up to 20 MB, their type told again from the copied bytes; text, a screenshot or both are needed (else code `empty`); once kept, any failure gives `paste-needed`. The content starts `sideby message <id> from <sender Session Label>` (or `from the user via sideby`), then the text, then `Screenshot: <path>` per screenshot. The sender is the Live Session among the command's parent processes. A Codex session (step 4) gets it through `codex queue --thread <session id> --message <pasteText>` run with that Account's launch environment (Hijack Variables cleared, `CODEX_HOME` set; the queued text is the paste line, never the Message text; 20 s timeout; Codex's output ignored): exit 0 gives `delivered` with a `note` that it is read when the current turn ends, anything else `paste-needed`. Grok Build, pi, a guessed session, a `crossSessionInbound: "refuse"` account or any failure give `paste-needed` with `pasteText` ("Read the message sideby kept for you at <file> (sideby message <id>) …") put on the clipboard and a plain `note`; a Claude target that holds messages (`crossSessionInbound` `hold`, or not `accept` while the session is in bypass permission mode, from the transcript's last `permission-mode` record, else `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` in its arguments) gets a `note` to approve it within 5 minutes or run `sideby messages inbound accept`. Output `{ message: { id, to, toSessionId, toAccount, from?, status: stored|delivered|read|paste-needed, file, attachments[], pasteText, note?, sentAt }, copied }`. Exit 0; 1 no session, several, bad image, or the sender's own session.
- `sideby messages [--to <acct|session>] [--limit <n>] [--json]`: kept Messages newest first (20 by default), `{ messages: [receipt] }`; a `delivered` or `paste-needed` one becomes `read` when `sideby message <id>` shows in the last 256 KB of the target's transcript (only lines with it are read; the status is saved in the receipt, never in a Host file). A receipt with `needsApproval: true` (ADR-0045) was delivered but waits for approval in the target's terminal; the field goes once it is read, and after 6 minutes unread the status becomes `paste-needed`. Panel: `/api/messages/inbound` (read), `/api/messages/inbound/accept` and `/undo` (writes; refused by a read-only Panel).
- `sideby messages inbound [accept|undo] [--yes] [--json]`: per Claude settings file, `state` accept|hold|refuse|default|other|missing|blocked of the top-level `crossSessionInbound`. `accept` writes `"accept"` only where it is default or hold (recording whether the key was there and its exact old value), with the same rules as `remote-control` (preview and exit 10 without `--yes`, `writeIfUnchanged`, other keys kept, a link written at its real target, no settings.json created); `refuse` and any other value are never changed and are named with the reason (a run that changes nothing has `ok` false and exits 1); `undo` restores the old value while the key still holds `"accept"` from sideby. Output `{ action: status|accept|undo, applied?, groups?, leftAlone?, results?, message? }`; an accept preview gives each group `change: { key: "crossSessionInbound", from: <value now, or null when not set>, to: "accept" }` and lists in `leftAlone` the files it never changes, each with `reason`. `sideby doctor` warns `messages.inbound-held` (not fixable by `--fix`) for a Claude account that starts in bypass mode (its alias or config `accounts.<ref>.args`, or `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in its settings) while `crossSessionInbound` is not accept or refuse.
- `sideby edit <acct> [--path] [--json]` (spec §3.30, ADR-0033): open the account's Host settings file (`FamilyDef.settingsFile`: claude and pi `settings.json`, codex and grok `config.toml`) with the system's default program: macOS `/usr/bin/open -t`, WSL `cmd.exe /c start "" <path>` with the `wslpath -w` path (a path with `&|<>^%"` is refused), other Linux `xdg-open`. Reads none of the file and never creates or changes it. Output `{ ref, family, file, path, target?, sharedWith[], opened, command? }`: `target` is the real file when `path` is a link, `sharedWith` the other accounts of the Family whose file is the same. `--path` only reports (`opened: false`). Exit 0; 1 with code `no-settings-file`, `settings-missing` (also a dangling link), `open-failed`; 2 missing argument.
- `sideby browser [--enable|--disable] [--yes] [--json]` and `sideby browser open <acct> [--profile <folder|name|email>] [--json]` (spec §3.24, ADR-0023, Google Chrome on macOS, and in WSL the Chrome installed on Windows): Browser Sign-ins, off until config `browser.signIns` is true (`--enable` shows what is read, exit 10; `--yes` writes it). While on, sideby reads only `Local State` (each profile's folder, display name and, when it is an email, `user_name`: the Google account it uses in Chrome) and the Local Storage key names (never values) of `https://claude.ai`, `https://chatgpt.com`, `https://grok.com` and each plugin Family's `website.match.origin`; never cookies, Login Data, IndexedDB or the Keychain, no network. A profile signed in to an Account when a key name holds, as a whole segment, Claude's `oauthAccount.accountUuid` or Codex's `id_token` claim `chatgpt_user_id` (else `user_id`), Grok's `auth.json` `user_id`, or the id a plugin Family's `website.match.signInId` returns (`_` separates segments); the ids are compared in memory and never output. Output `{ enabled, browser, found, profiles: [{ dir, name, email?, signIns: [ref], changedAt? }], families: { matched, openOnly }, sites: { family: url }, choices: { ref: dir }, problems }`, newest change first; a match may be left from before a sign-out. When one account shows up in several profiles, only those whose `email` is the account's login email stay; an account found nowhere gets the one profile whose `email` is its login email (this also covers plugin Families without `website.match`, which are `openOnly`). `sideby browser set <acct> <folder|name|email> [--json]` saves the user's own choice in config `browser.choices` (ref → folder), which replaces the finding (the account is in that profile's `signIns` alone) and is what `open` uses; `--auto` removes it; output `{ ref, profile: { dir, name } | null, changed }`, exit 0, or 1 with `no-website`, `no-profiles`, `profile-unknown`, `profile-ambiguous`; only sideby's config is written. A choice whose folder is gone is skipped and named in `problems`. `open` runs `/usr/bin/open -na <Chrome.app> --args --profile-directory=<dir> <url>` (in WSL: `cmd.exe /d /c start "" <chrome.exe> --profile-directory=<dir> <url>`, folders from one `cmd.exe /d /c echo %LOCALAPPDATA%...` call) (claude.ai, chatgpt.com, grok.com, a plugin Family's `website.url`) for the only matching profile or `--profile`; output `{ ref, url, profile: { dir, name }, command }`. Exit 0; 1 with code `unsupported`, `no-website`, `not-installed`, `no-profiles`, `profile-needed`, `profile-unknown`, `profile-ambiguous`, `open-failed`. The Panel shows the matched browser user's Google account (else its name) after each account's email; a click opens it.
- `sideby app install [--url <url>] [--json]`: panel launcher that runs `ui --background` (or opens `<url>`): macOS `~/Applications/sideby.app` (bundle id `dev.sideby.panel`), Linux `~/.local/share/applications/sideby.desktop`. Records the current Node and sideby paths; `sideby update` runs it again, so run it yourself only after upgrading Node or installing sideby another way. Without `--url` it keeps an address an earlier `--url` install recorded (uninstall, then install, to drop it). `sideby app uninstall [--json]` removes only files it created. Exit 0; 1 on an unsupported platform or a foreign file in the way.
- Library: `createPanelHandler({ runtime, basePath?, allowedHosts, readOnly?, theme?, lang?, updates? })` mounts the panel in another local Node server. `theme` is `{ colorScheme?: 'auto'|'light'|'dark', header?: 'plain'|'bar', light?: PanelThemeTokens, dark?: PanelThemeTokens }`; tokens (for example `font`, `bg`, `surface`, `primary`, `onPrimary`, `radius`, `controlHeight`, `gutter`; full list in `src/panel/theme.ts`) become CSS custom properties in the nonce'd style. Unknown tokens and values with characters outside letters, digits, spaces and `# % ( ) , . + - / ' " _` throw a TypeError. `lang` is `'auto'|'en'|'zh'` (default `auto`: the language picked in the panel, then the browser's); `en` or `zh` wins and hides the panel's language switch, and any other value throws a TypeError. It is read when the handler is created; create it again to switch. `updates` (default true) shows the update label, dialog and Auto Update switch; `false` hides them and refuses `/api/update*` with 403. `<basePath>/icon.svg` serves the sideby mark for a Portal's tab; `<basePath>/favicon.svg` the small cut.
- `sideby shell-init zsh|bash`: one shell function per account (`sideby-<family>-<name>`) plus config `aliases`, each calling `sideby run '<alias>'` so the config stays the source (commands that take an account, such as `run` and `doctor`, also accept an alias). Use `eval "$(sideby shell-init zsh)"`. `sideby shell-init [zsh|bash] --write` rewrites the configured `shellInitFile` with that output (exit 1 when none is configured or a file was not written; a file whose first line is not the shell-init header is never overwritten).
- `sideby resume <family> [-- host args]`: what the Host-named shell function calls. When the arguments resume a session by UUID (Claude and Grok `--resume <id>`, `--resume=<id>`, `-r <id>`; Codex `resume <id>`), start the non-main Account that holds it (Claude `projects/*/<id>.jsonl`, Codex `sessions/**/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl`, Grok `sessions/*/<id>/`; newest write wins) exactly as `run` would, with a note on stderr. When no Account holds a Claude session but one started it (`session-env/<id>/`; the session never got a message), drop the by-id resume and start a new session in that Account (`run` for a non-main one, the Host with only those arguments removed for the Main Account), with a note on stderr (ADR-0009). Otherwise, or when the Family's select variable is already set, run the Host unchanged. Exit: the Host's code; 1 for an unknown Family or one that cannot route (pi). With config `resumeRouting: true`, `shell-init` also prints `function <bin> { … }` for each routable Family that has a non-main Account, unless an Alias has that name; it calls `sideby resume` only when the select variable is unset and an argument is UUID-shaped (or `--resume=<uuid>`), otherwise the Host directly.
- `sideby plugins [--json]`: loaded plugins and load errors. Exit 0; 1 if any failed.
- `sideby update [--yes] [--json]` (spec §3.23, ADR-0021): ask the npm registry now for the `latest` sideby and show `current`, `latest`, `available`, `method` (`kind` npm, pnpm, bun, volta, npx, project, source or local, a Local Build from `pnpm local` in a checkout whose `command` is `pnpm local --off`; `canUpdate`, `reason`, `reasonCode`, `reasonAt`), `command`, `canRun`, `releaseNotes`. Up to date: exit 0. Without `--yes`: exit 10 (ask the user first). With `--yes`: run `command` (npm, pnpm or bun global installs only), restart a running background panel (`restartedPanel`), run `sideby app install` again from the new version when the desktop app is installed (`refreshedApp`), exit 0; `skillUpdate` (`installed`, `outdated`, `command`, `canRun`, `reason`, `reasonCode`) is the installed sideby skill, which the Update brings along with `npx -y skills update sideby -g -y` (`skillUpdated` in the result; with the CLI current, `sideby update` offers the skill alone); a skill in a git repository is left alone unless the skills tool's `.skill-lock.json` records installing it there (`canRun: false`, `reasonCode: skill-in-git`, give the user `command`). `canRun: false` exits 1: give the user `command` to run. Registry unreachable or install failed: exit 1. Update Check: once a day, after a command on a terminal (never with `--json`), sideby asks `<registry>/-/package/sideby/dist-tags` (`SIDEBY_UPDATE_REGISTRY` overrides the registry) in a detached process and prints one stderr line on a later run; every `--json` output then carries `_notice.update` (`current`, `latest`, `command: "sideby update"`), and `_notice.skill` (`command: "sideby update"`) when the installed sideby skill is for another version: finish the task, mention it once, and offer to update (run `sideby update --json`, then `--yes` after the user agrees); off with `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, `SIDEBY_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, config `update.check: false`, CI or a Local Build. Config `update.auto: true` (off by default; do not turn it on unless asked) installs a newer version of the same major after the check when no `sideby run`, `next` or `resume` is running, together with the skill, and brings a skill behind a current sideby up to date by itself; with it off, a terminal gets one line a day while the skill is behind.
- Auto Handoff (config `handoff`, spec §3.17): `auto` (default false; alone it hands over only to other families' accounts listed in `order`), `sameFamily` (default false; also the same family, the kind vendors may act on), `otherFamilies` (default false; other families' subscription accounts take over when the origin's family has none that can, family by family in `familyOrder`, each by most quota left), `familyOrder` (family ids), `api` (default false; API accounts of any family take over last, billed per use, sideby caps no spending; ADR-0046), `prepareAt` 80, `threshold` 95 (Quota Pressure in percent), `adaptive` true (each window hands over when it has less room than 1.5 times its largest turn of the run's last 5, between `prepareAt` and 99; before a turn is measured, or with false, at `threshold`; ADR-0032), `waitIfResetWithinMinutes` 30 (waits only when the session continues by itself at the reset: Claude with `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` not false in the account's `settings.json`; Codex and Grok never wait; the user sees a `systemMessage` at the threshold and a desktop notification at the limit, and `! sideby handoff ready` typed in the session moves on at once), `countdownSeconds` 10, `crossOrganization` (refs or aliases that may take over from another organization; organizations are compared by `org`, else email domain), `families.<family>`: `{ policy: "pressure"|"order", order: [ref|alias] }`. Only interactive sessions that sideby started, with stdin a TTY and a `sideby` on PATH that answers `sideby handoff-hook --check` with `ok` (sideby's arguments go before the user's first `--`); an account more than `threshold − 10` used (the Takeover Limit, 85 by default; also for `sideby next`) counts as full; when none may take over, the reason names the setting that would allow one; an account of the origin's same login is skipped, also when `order` names it, and the terminal says why; never headless runs, Codex `--remote`, Grok `strict` or custom sandbox profiles. sideby stays the Host's parent: it sets `SIDEBY_HANDOFF_RUN`, `SIDEBY_HANDOFF_FAMILY`, `SIDEBY_HANDOFF_DIR` and adds hooks (Claude `--settings <state>/handoff/claude-settings.json`, Codex `-c hooks.PostToolUse=…`/`-c hooks.Stop=…`, Grok a hook file from `handoff setup`). The hidden `sideby handoff-hook <family> <event>` (PostToolUse, Stop, StopFailure) asks the session to write its brief at `prepareAt`, to finish when a window reaches its level (the message names the window, its percent and reset time; the brief counts as finished only with the last line `<!-- handoff brief complete -->`), and writes `ready.json`; a StopFailure counts only for a used-up quota, never a transient rate limit. sideby then ends the Host (SIGTERM, 10 s grace, never SIGKILL), finishes the brief (adds branch, uncommitted files, diff stat; assembles one from the session's records when needed), counts down (Enter stays and resumes the old session), and starts the next account with `--add-dir <chain dir>` (Claude, Codex) and the brief's path as the first prompt after `--`. Files: `<state>/handoffs/<chain>/` (mode 700; `plan.json`, `run-<id>.json`, `ready.json`, `request.json`, `waiting.json`, `chain.json`, `<n>-<ref>.md` briefs, mode 600). Starts: Claude (quota and limit; needs `quota setup claude`), Codex (quota; trust the hooks once per account in `/hooks`), Grok (quota and limit; needs `handoff setup grok` and `doctor grok --fix`; sandbox `off`/`devbox` start, `workspace`/`read-only` only receive). pi only receives. Plugin families can only receive.
- `sideby handoff rules [--json]`: read-only, every rule in effect: `{ auto, rules[{ id, params, settings, text }], apiUndecided, takeover[] }`; ids `when`, `windows`, `takeover`, `wait`, `sameFamily`, `otherFamilies`, `api`, `organization`, `order` (one per family with `policy: order`), `countdown`; `settings` names the `handoff` keys that change each. `apiUndecided`: Auto Handoff is on, API accounts exist and `handoff.api` is not set (they took over before ADR-0046): ask the user once and set it. `sideby handoff status [--json]`: read-only readiness: `auto`, `sameFamily`, `prepareAt`, `threshold`, `apiUndecided`, `sideby: { ok, problem? }` (the `sideby` on PATH can run the hook), `families[]` (`family`, `starts`, `ready`, `problems[]`, `notes[]`, `order: { policy, order, unknown[] }`), `nextSteps[]` (commands in order). Exit 0. `sideby handoff enable [--same-family] [--no-same-family] [--other-ai|--no-other-ai] [--ai-order <family,…>] [--api|--no-api] [--order <family>=<acct,…>] [--prepare-at n] [--threshold n] [--wait-minutes n] [--countdown n] [--yes] [--json]` / `sideby handoff disable [--yes] [--json]`: change only the config `handoff` key (other settings kept): exit 10 with the change shown (`diff`), 0 once written or already so, 1 for an unknown `--order` account (`code: unknown-account`); `--json`: `{ applied, file, diff, settings, nextSteps }`. Agents run `status`, then `enable` and ask before `--yes`, then each `nextSteps` entry. With Auto Handoff off, `sideby run` prints a one-line pointer to `handoff status` at most once a day when the account ended past the threshold, and the Panel shows a hint and an Auto Handoff dialog (`/api/handoff/status`, `/api/handoff/configure` with `confirm`).
- `sideby handoff ready [--to <account>] [--brief <file>] [--json]`: inside a session sideby started with Auto Handoff, hand over to the next account when this turn ends; prints (JSON `next`) the account that takes over, which can differ from `sideby next` because the chain never goes back to an account it used; `--to` names the account, also one the chain already used (hand back), and fails with `no-pick` rather than picking another; `--brief` copies the user's own note into the chain directory; a manual request never waits for a reset, and while the session waits for its quota (`waiting.json`) it hands over at once (JSON `now: true`). Exit 0; 1 outside such a session (`code: not-in-handoff-run`) or when the brief cannot be read (`brief-unreadable`). `sideby handoff setup <family> [--yes] [--json]` / `teardown`: the hook file for a Host without a launch option (Grok): exit 10 when it only showed the change; teardown removes the file only while unchanged. Exit 1 also when no account can take over now (`no-pick`; nothing is written). Doctor warns (`handoff.no-quota-tap`, `handoff.setup-missing`, `handoff.order-empty`, `handoff.order-unknown`) only when `handoff.auto` is on.
- `sideby families [family] [--json]`: each loaded family (plugins included): `layout` (`main`, `account` relative to HOME), `selectVar`, `login` (`args` or null, `hint`), `quota`, `usage`, `quotaSetup`, and `shared[]` (`path`, `mode`, `key?`, `mainPath?`, `credential?`, `noSymlink?`, `source` `family`|`config`, `meaning`: one fixed sentence on what the item is in each account). Exit 0; 1 unknown family; 2 more than one family.
- `sideby <command> --help` (or `sideby help <command>`) prints help with examples for `new`, `alias`, `login`, `doctor` and `families`; other commands print the general help.
- Any command: exit 2 on a usage error (unknown option, missing argument); 1 when sideby fails (unknown account, invalid config); 10 when a change was shown and needs confirmation (`quota setup`, `handoff setup`, `update` or `browser --enable|--disable` without `--yes`).

## JSON contract

- `list`, `new`, `next`, `alias` (also `alias list`), `doctor`, `quota` (with `setup`/`teardown`), `handoff`, `families`, `plugins` `app`, `desktop`, `sessions`, `history`, `send` and `messages` accept `--json`; `run`, `resume`, `login`, `ui` and `shell-init` do not.
- Every JSON output has `schemaVersion: 1`. Adding fields keeps the version; removing, renaming or changing meaning bumps it. With `--json`, errors print `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "error": "...", "code": "..." }`: `code` is `usage` for a malformed command line, a reason such as `no-quota-source`, `no-accounts` or `alias-invalid`, or `error`.
- JSON Schemas for each output and for the config file ship in the package under `schemas/` (`list`, `new`, `next`, `alias`, `alias-list`, `shell-init-setup`, `doctor`, `quota`, `quota-setup`, `quota-teardown`, `handoff-status`, `handoff-rules`, `handoff-enable`, `handoff-disable`, `handoff-ready`, `handoff-setup`, `handoff-teardown`, `families`, `plugins`, `app-install`, `app-uninstall`, `desktop`, `error`, `config`).
- `list --json`: `families[]` (`id`, `title`, `bin`, `installUrl`, `installCommand?`, `installed`, `brokenBin?`, `plugin`), `accounts[]` (`family`, `name`, `ref`, `dir`, `isMain`, `kind` `subscription`|`api`, `secretFile?`, `familyTitle`, `hostInstalled`, `login` `logged-in`|`logged-out`|`unknown`|`not-needed`, `model?`, `problems?` string[], `desktopApp?` { `app`, `installed`, `running` } on macOS for subscription accounts of claude and codex), `pluginErrors[]` (`where`, `message`).
- `doctor --json`: `status` `ok`|`issues`, `accounts[]` (`ref`, `family`, `name`, `kind`, `dir`, `shared` {`ok`, `total`}, `backups`, `findings[]`), `general[]`, `fixes[]` (`account`, `item`, `code`, `ok`, `message`). `shared` counts only items the Main Account has.
- Finding: `level` (`ok`|`warn`|`fail`), `account`, `item`, `code` (stable, e.g. `link.real-file`, `link.other-target` (warn), `link.dangling` (fail), `symlink-forbidden` (fail; any link where the item must be a real file or copy), `path.invalid`, `missing`, `copy.stale`, `symlink-forbidden`, `credential.mode`, `json-key.drift`, `json-key.would-remove`, `name.backup-like`, `plugin.error`, `skill.outdated`), `message`, `hint?`, `source` (`core` or plugin name), `fixable`. sideby never re-points a link.
- Quota: `status: "ok"` with `windows[]` (`label` `5h`|`7d`|`<n>m`, `windowMinutes`, `usedPercent`, `resetsAt`), `observedAt`, `source`, `plan?`, `from?` (the account the reading was taken from, when another account of the same login); or `status: "unavailable"` with `reason` `not-enabled`|`no-session`|`unrecognized`|`no-source`|`api-account` and `detail?`.
- Usage: `status: "ok"` with `days`, `sessions`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `totalTokens`, optional `daily[]` (`{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", totalTokens }`, one per local day ending today, oldest first, 0 for days without records; can sum to less than `totalTokens`) and optional `lastActivityAt` (ISO, newest record read); or `unavailable` with `reason` `no-source`|`no-session`|`unrecognized` and `detail?`. Sources: Claude `projects/**/*.jsonl`, Codex `sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`; Grok and pi have none.
- `new --json`: `{ ok, account, steps[], hookErrors[], nextSteps[], alias?: { name, added, message? }, shellInitFiles?: [{ shell, path, ok, action?: "written"|"unchanged", message? }], suggestion?: { name, alias?, aliasProblem? } }` (`suggestion` only with `--next`).
- `next --json`: `{ family, pick: ref|null, accounts[] (`ref`, `kind`, `state`, `pressure`: number|null, `resetsAt?` for full, `observedAt?`, `quotaFrom?`, `sameLoginAs?`: the current account when this one is its same login, never picked), from?: the current account (`SIDEBY_ACCOUNT`), hasQuota, earliestReset?: { ref, at } }`, best first.
- `alias add|rm --json`: `{ ok, alias, status: "added"|"exists"|"removed"|"absent", account?, args?, shellInitFiles? }`; `ok` is false when a shell-init file was not rewritten.
- `app install --json`: `{ platform, path, files[], mode: "panel"|"url", url?, node, entry, updated, hints[] }`; `app uninstall --json`: `{ platform, removed[], skipped[] (path, reason) }`.
- `quota setup|teardown --json`: setup `{ family, applied, plan: { status: "enabled"|"ready"|"blocked", file, diff, message } }`; teardown `{ family, ok, message, diff? }` (`schemas/quota-setup.json`, `schemas/quota-teardown.json`).
- No output ever contains a credential value.

## Configuration

- File: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/sideby/config.json` (optional). Fields: `accounts.<ref>.args`, `aliases` (`<short>` → ref, or `{ account, args? }`), `ignore`, `pluginDirs`, `plugins.<name>` (`enabled` plus plugin settings), `extraSharedItems.<family>[]` (`path` relative to the account directory, no `..`; `mode`; optional `noSymlink`, `credential`), `shellInitFile` (`{ zsh?, bash? }`, absolute or `~/` paths sideby keeps equal to `sideby shell-init <shell>`), `resumeRouting` (boolean, default false; Host-named functions that route a resume by id, see `sideby resume`), `accountTitle` (boolean, default false; terminal title `[<SIDEBY_LABEL>]` at launch), `claudeMod` (boolean, default true; load sideby's Claude Code mod with `--plugin-dir`), `display` (`{ families?: [id], accounts?: { <family>: [name] }, pinned?: { <family>: [name] } }`, the Display Order and Pinned Accounts the Panel's arrange mode and pin menu write; `list` and `quota` follow it, pinned first, then listed, the rest after in their usual order; `list --json` marks pinned accounts `pinned: true`; display only, never the Handoff Order), `quota.check.<family>` (boolean, default true; false stops quota checks that cost a request, such as Grok's), `panel` (`{ theme?: system|light|dark, language?: auto|en|zh }`).
- State: `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/sideby/` (quota cache, last doctor result, original `settings.json` bytes).
- Plugins directory: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/sideby/plugins/`.
- Share Modes: `link`, `copy`, `link-or-copy`, `link-or-local`, `local`, `local-if-api`, `info`, `json-key`.

## Plugin API

- A plugin is a local directory with `plugin.json` (`name`, `version`, `description`, optional `main`, `userConfig`) and `index.ts` exporting `{ name, register(api) } satisfies Plugin`.
- Loaded from built-ins, then `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/sideby/plugins/*`, then config `pluginDirs`. Directory, `plugin.json` and entry must be owned by the user and not group/other writable.
- A plugin is local code with the user's full permissions.
- Only `import type { Plugin } from 'sideby'`; never import values. Everything arrives through `api`.
- `api.family(def: FamilyDef)`: register a Family (`id`, `title`, `bin`, `installUrl`, `layout`, `selectVar`, `hijackVars`, `apiVars`, `sharedItems`, `login`, optional `logo`, `website`, `secretFileMeansApi`, `defaultArgs`, `keepTitle` (`{ args, key }`: Host args that keep the `accountTitle` title, skipped when a user arg contains `key`), `loginState`, `model`, `readQuota`, `readUsage`, `quotaSetup`). A throwing `loginState` or `model` becomes an entry in that account's `problems`.
- `website: { url, match?: { origin, signInId(account) } }` (ADR-0043): the vendor website for Browser Sign-ins; `url` https with no query or fragment, `origin` https with no path; `signInId` returns an id (8+ chars) the website puts in its Local Storage key names, compared in memory only. Without `match`, the user picks the browser user. Invalid: dropped with a plugin error (`website.invalid`).
- `logo: { path, color?, title?, fillRule? }`: the panel's mark for the Family, one SVG path in a 24x24 view box. `path` holds only SVG path data (max 20000 chars), `color` is hex. An invalid logo is dropped with a plugin error; the panel then shows initials.
- `api.on('launch.before', [filter], handler)`: before `run`/`login`; mutate `ctx.env` and `ctx.args`, or `throw api.abort(msg)`. 30 s timeout.
- `api.on('account.create.before', [filter], handler)`: before `new` (CLI or panel) writes anything; `ctx` is `{ family, name, api, accounts, config }` (`accounts`: the family's existing accounts). `throw api.abort(msg)` refuses: the CLI exits 1 with `msg`, the panel answers 400 `{ error, code: 'create-refused' }`. Any other error or the 10 s timeout also stops creation. 10 s.
- `api.on('account.created', [filter], handler)`: after `new`; `ctx.log()` for next steps. 30 s.
- `api.on('doctor.check', [filter], handler)`: return `CheckResult[]` (`level`, `item`, `code`, `message`, `hint?`, `fix?`). 10 s.
- `filter` is `{ family?: string }`. `ctx.config` is the plugin's own settings. `api.fs.writeFileAtomic(path, data, mode?)` for fixes.
- Built-in optional plugin `account-script`: when enabled, runs `<account>/sideby-before-launch` before each launch (25 s limit; failure stops the launch).
- Test plugins with `sideby/testing`: `withFakeHome`, `fakeHost`, `readHostLog`, `snapshot`, `diffSnapshots`.

## Panel settings through the CLI

- `sideby pin|unpin <account|short command> [--json]`: Same Login together, at most 3 per Family; new pins go last; repeated operations are no-ops. JSON: `ref`, `pinned`, `changed`, `message`, `display` (schemas/pin.json, schemas/unpin.json).
- `sideby order [--json]`: `display` and effective `families` with account `name`, `ref`, `pinned` (schemas/order.json). `order <family> <name>...`, `order --families <id>...`, `order --reset` save immediately; reset keeps pins. Unknown or repeated names fail; stale names are removed on write. Display only, not Handoff Order.
- `sideby quota check <family> on|off [--json]`: saves the fetching switch; JSON `family`, `on`, `changed` (schemas/quota-check.json). Local reading continues; CI blocks fetching. `quota [account|family] --refresh` works for every fetching Family.
- `sideby local [on|off] [--yes] [--json]` (ADR-0024, for sideby developers): `running` (`local`, `npm` or null), `local` (the kept Local Build: `version`, `commit`, `dirty`, `builtAt`), `kept` (npm version set aside), `switched` (schemas/local.json). No argument: status, exit 0. `on` links the kept Local Build (no rebuild; `pnpm local` builds), `off` restores the kept npm package or installs `latest`, then runs `sideby update --skill --yes` of the npm code so the skill comes along (`skillSynced`); without `--yes` exit 10, with it switch, restart a background panel (`restartedPanel`), exit 0. `blocked` (exit 1): no Local Build, or not an npm global install.
- `sideby update --skill [--yes] [--json]`: update only the installed sideby skill to this sideby's version; never installs the CLI and asks no registry (says `sideby update` is separate when the last check saw a newer sideby). Without `--yes` exit 10; with it exit 0, or 1 when the skill update failed.
- `sideby update --auto on|off [--json]`: saves Auto Update without checking/installing; JSON `auto`, `changed` (schemas/update-auto.json). Exit 0, no preview; enable only when asked.
- `sideby handoff rules --json` (new, schemas/handoff-rules.json); `handoff status --json` adds `apiUndecided`; handoff settings add `otherFamilies`, `familyOrder`, `api` (ADR-0046); schemaVersion remains 1.
- `sideby handoff status --json`: additive `overview` with `settings`, `takeover` decisions and `recent` hand-overs (schemas/handoff-status.json); schemaVersion remains 1.
- Agent instructions: skills/sideby/references/panel.md covers Display Order, pins, model and Remote Control; quota.md, update.md and handoff.md cover the other settings.

AI Tasks (ADR-0027):
- sideby ask [<text>] [--task free|fix|quota|account|host|plugin|terminal|handoff|menubar|hotkey] [--account <ref>] [--terminal <id>] [--attach <file>]... [--print] [--json]: opens the user's terminal, which runs this Node and sideby by absolute path; --print only prints the prompt; --attach (repeatable, at most 5) adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image up to 20 MB or an MP4, MOV or WebM video up to 200 MB, type from the file's first bytes (refused: code attachment-type, attachment-too-large, too-many-attachments, attachment-link, attachment-missing), copied to `ai/attachments/<task-id>/` (deleted after 7 days) and listed in the prompt; `--json` gives `attachments: [{ path, kind, bytes }]`; Codex (`FamilyDef.imageArg`) also gets each image as `--image=<path>`; --account (an API account too) becomes `ask.account`, the next default. Exit 1 gives a paste command or prompt, with `reason` (a code: no-accounts, none-signed-in, all-full, not-installed, automation-denied, npx-cache, unsafe-path, failed, unsupported-platform) and `detail` (what to do next). npx-cache: install sideby with `npm i -g sideby` first.
- sideby ask --run <id>: consumes a private task file (expires after one hour), starts the Host in sideby's AI work directory. A prompt task starts as `sideby run` would, but never with the Host's permission checks switched off (ADR-0031, `FamilyDef.aiTaskArgs`): Claude Code drops `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` and gets `--permission-mode auto` unless another mode is picked; Codex drops `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and `--yolo`; other families start unchanged. `sideby run` keeps every argument. The text output after opening a terminal adds "Its permission checks stay on, so risky actions are checked first." for such a family.
- sideby ask --spec - [--print] --json (ADR-0030): a Portal starts an AI Task with a Task Spec, one JSON object on stdin (at most 1 MB, never through a shell): `{ specVersion: 1, prompt, cwd?, ... }` (another Tool's Task Prompt; keys stripped again, attachments section appended; `cwd` an existing folder inside HOME by real path, else exit 1 `bad-cwd`; no `cwd` = sideby's task folder, declared as `"cwd": "engine"`) or `{ specVersion: 1, native: { task, text?, context? }, ... }` (sideby's own task, prompt unchanged). Both take lang (en|zh), account, terminal, remember, files (absolute paths, at most 5). Output as `sideby ask --json`; --print gives `{ schemaVersion, prompt, removedSecrets }` (schemas/ask-print.json) and writes nothing. Refused: `{ schemaVersion, error, code, reason }` with spec-invalid, spec-too-large, bad-cwd (exit 1) or spec-version (exit 2: update sideby).
- sideby ask --choices --json: `{ account, accounts: [{ ref, label, signedIn }], terminal, terminals: [{ id, label }], reason, detail }` (schemas/ask-choices.json); account null with reason no-accounts|none-signed-in|all-full.
- createPanelHandler({ ask: { bridge: 'postMessage' } }) (ADR-0030): inside a frame, hides the Panel's "Let AI do it" button and every AI Task entry posts `{ type: 'local-tools:ask', version: 1, preset, native: { task, text, context }, text }` to window.parent at the Panel's own origin. The package root's ai-tasks.json declares sideby's tasks for a Portal (skill, skillInstall, cwd "engine", contribute, one native preset per task with en/zh title, placeholder, examples).
- sideby terminal [--set <id>|--custom '<template>'|--unset] [--json]: terminal discovery and preference. --custom saves terminal.custom (an argv template with both {cmd} and {cwd}) and selects it; --set custom needs one saved. Config terminal.preferred, terminal.custom, ask.account select the defaults.
- sideby key <account> [--var <NAME>] [--json]: hidden TTY input; never send a key to an AI. An empty key writes nothing (exit 1). API accounts and families with secretFileMeansApi: false only.
- sideby try <account> [--yes] [--json]: a short paid Host request, with the same arguments as `sideby run` plus the probe's. Exit 10 asks for confirmation; --yes returns 0/1 with redacted output.
- sideby plugins new <id> [--json]: local Family Plugin skeleton. Plugins run with the user's full permissions.
- sideby plugins check <id|path> [--json]: deterministic validation, exit 0/1, each problem includes a fix.
Schemas: ask.json, terminal.json, key.json, try.json, plugins-new.json, plugins-check.json. All include schemaVersion: 1.

Settings (spec §3.29, ADR-0029):
- sideby autostart [on|off] [--yes] [--json]: start the panel in the background at login (macOS LaunchAgent `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.sideby.panel.plist`, mode 644, `RunAtLoad` true, `KeepAlive` false, ProgramArguments = this Node, this sideby's entry, `ui --background --no-open`, a sideby marker comment). JSON: `supported`, `reason?`, `state` (off, on, stale: a recorded path is gone and `missing` names it, foreign: a file sideby did not write, never touched), `path`, `programArguments?`, `current` (it starts this sideby), and for on/off `action`, `changed`, `applied`, `content?`, `commands` (`launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>`, `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/dev.sideby.panel`), `loaded?`, `note?`. Without --yes a change exits 10; refused exits 1 with code unsupported, foreign, npx-cache, temp-dir or unsafe-path (install with `npm i -g sideby` first). `sideby update` (`refreshedAutostart`) and `pnpm local` rewrite an existing agent; neither creates one.
- sideby menubar [on|off] [--yes] [--json] (spec §3.31, ADR-0034): quota in the macOS menu bar. LaunchAgent `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.sideby.menubar.plist` (marker, mode 644, `KeepAlive` restarts only after a failed exit) running `/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript -e <menu script> <node> <entry>`; same JSON, refusals, exit 10 and update/`pnpm local` refresh as `autostart`. Off by default. `sideby menubar snapshot [--lang en|zh] --json`: what the menu shows: `title` (percent of the account `sideby next` picks, highest across Families; empty without data), `level` (ok, warn ≥60, fail ≥85, none), `tooltip`, `updatedAt`, `lang`, `sections[]` (`family`, `title`, `rows[]`: `ref`, `label`, `detail`, `level`, `recommended`, `tip`), `labels`. `sideby menubar start <account> --json`: opens the account in the Preferred Terminal (`task`, `account`, `terminal`, `opened`, `command`, `reason?`, `detail?`). Config menubar.hotkey (default `opt+x`, `off`) toggles the menu from anywhere; snapshot field `hotkey`. `sideby menubar --json` adds `loaded` (false: on but launchd is not running it; `menubar on --yes` loads it again), `icon.visible` (false: macOS put the icon behind « in a full menu bar; null: no report in 15 minutes) and `hotkey` (`keys`, `label`, `enabled`, `isDefault`, `registered` true/false/null, `problem?`). `sideby menubar hotkey [<keys>|off|default] --json`: shows it, or checks (needs opt, cmd or ctrl; codes `hotkey.invalid`, `hotkey.needs-modifier`, `hotkey.reserved`), writes config and tells a running item through the distributed notification `dev.sideby.menubar.reload`, no restart (`changed`, `nudged`, `hotkey`). The script reports registration with `menubar snapshot --hotkey ok|taken --hotkey-label <label>` and its icon with `--icon visible|hidden`.
- sideby config get [<key>] [--json]: without a key, `file` and `keys` (`key` dot path with `<…>` placeholders, `meaning`, `takes`, `value?`, `entries?`); with one, `key`, `set`, `value?`, `meaning`, `takes`.
- sideby config set <key> <value> [--yes] [--json] / config unset <key> [--yes] [--json]: value is JSON when it parses, else text. The whole result must match schemas/config.json (else code bad-value); unknown keys bad-key; `plugins.<name>` settings refused (plugin-config) except `plugins.<name>.enabled`; `accounts.<ref>.args` takes only model and effort arguments. JSON `action`, `key`, `file`, `changed`, `applied`, `before?`, `after?`. Without --yes a change exits 10. Config `panel.theme` (system, light, dark) and `panel.language` (auto, en, zh) are the Panel's appearance.
Schemas: autostart.json, menubar.json, menubar-snapshot.json, menubar-start.json, menubar-hotkey.json, config-get.json, config-set.json.

- Codex quota (ADR-0038): official `codex app-server`, `account/rateLimits/read`, every 15 minutes or on `sideby quota codex --refresh --json`; `quota.check.codex: false` and CI disable querying. Select the `codex` bucket. Local rollouts are fallback-only once a fetched answer exists (`QuotaFetch.localFallbackOnly`). Failures keep the previous observation and report `fetchError`. Menu rows expose `observedAt` and `stale`; the footer reports check time, not quota age. `sideby menubar snapshot --refresh --json` forces enabled Host queries.
